summary: Grays Harbor County, WA; 70-foot pole tower on the Clemons Tree Farm, built in the 1940s and removed about 1960. Footings reportedly remain; private land.

facts.status_note: Firetower.org says now gone; Weebly dates removal to c.1960 and WillhiteWeb says possibly the 1960s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Weebly gives c.1960 and its survey-station note says a lot was reported destroyed in 1960; WillhiteWeb says possibly the 1960s; firetower.org gives no date. Treated as about 1960, not confirmed.
Firetower.org and firelookout.com spell it Clemans; WillhiteWeb and HistoryLink spell it Clemons. The story uses Clemons.
Firetower.org calls the tower privately owned; WillhiteWeb says Weyerhaeuser built it. The story reports both, and HistoryLink confirms Weyerhaeuser's tree farm at the same place and period.

notes_for_editor: Brief location conflict: FFLOS coordinates (46.843669, -123.395497) and the west_us_lookouts figures (46.8276, -123.3796) are about 2 km apart. Not resolved here; the record keeps the FFLOS coordinates, which firetower.org gives. HistoryLink calls the tract's namesake Charles H. Clemons in one place and Charles L. Clemons in another, so the middle initial is unclear and the story omits it. The survey-station note concerns a station's lot and may not mean the tower was destroyed in 1960. The brief lists agency as Privately Owned; kept.
